ai_defects.title: pivot-then-immediately-resend: the faint replacement chooser re-sends the member the AI had just deliberately withdrawn at 13% HP
ai_defects.turn_evidence: act turn_before 1 -> turn_after 2. Board: Zapdos at 52/398 (it had absorbed three Surging Strikes crits on turn 1), Kyogre 419, bench Zamazenta 403 / Melmetal 492 / Marshadow 398 all untouched. The AI first switched Zapdos out for Lucario mid-turn ('CHAMPION~WALLACE withdrew Zapdos! CHAMPION~WALLACE sent out Lucario!'), which was correct. Raging Bolt's Thunderclap then KOd Kyogre in the same turn, and the faint replacement sent that same 52-HP Zapdos straight back in ('CHAMPION~WALLACE sent out Zapdos!'). Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash KOd it on turn 3.
ai_defects.better_action: answer the faint with Zamazenta or Melmetal and leave the 13%-HP Zapdos on the bench it was just moved to. The mid-turn pivot decision and the end-of-turn replacement decision do not appear to share state.
ai_defects.affected_paths: the faint-replacement chooser, not the pair AI. Any trainer whose AI pivots a low-HP member out and loses a partner in the same turn can repeat it.

ai_defects.title: Iron Defense chosen over an available guaranteed KO, and against an all-special board where Defence does nothing
ai_defects.turn_evidence: Turn 4: Zamazenta at 403/403 and +1 Def faced Kartana (260 HP, Grass/Steel, 2x to Fighting - Body Press at +1 is roughly 474, a guaranteed OHKO) and Gholdengo (a Ghost, immune to Body Press, attacking with Shadow Ball, i.e. special). It chose Iron Defense. The KO was still there on turn 5 and it took it, but the free turn let Kartana attempt its own guaranteed OHKO on Kyogre, which Kyogre had to spend a 1/3 consecutive Protect to survive. Turn 8 (final act): Zamazenta, already at +3 or better, faced a single 5-HP Gholdengo that it is physically immune to and that was attacking specially; it used Iron Defense again. Heavy Slam - its only move that can damage a Ghost - would have KOd outright.
ai_defects.better_action: Body Press on turn 4 for the immediate KO; Heavy Slam on turn 8 for the immediate KO. The setup score should be gated on (a) no KO already available and (b) at least one physical attacker on the opposing board.
ai_defects.affected_paths: the shared setup-move scoring, not a bespoke tactic. Every authored Iron Defense / Cosmic Power / Bulk Up owner can reach the same branch; the second case in particular (raising physical Defence against a board with no physical attacker left) is the one worth a focused regression.

is_this_now_the_hardest_fight_in_the_gam.support: Six completed optimized cap-100 attempts, six losses. The four parties that went 4-0 against the previous roster went 0-4 against this one (6-3, 6-3, 6-2, 6-4), and two parties built from scratch against the rebuilt roster's own crack line also lost (6-5 and 6-3). No other encounter in this block has produced an 0-for-6 against optimized preparation. The roster's structural claims all hold up in play: the weather cannot be taken while Kyogre stands, neither lead can be flinched, Body Press and Close Combat are answered only by a Ghost, and the two win conditions (Kyogre's spread special offence and Zamazenta's single-target physical offence) genuinely require opposite answers.

is_it_winnable_by_a_party_built_against_.answer: NOT DEMONSTRATED. The nearest miss was v3-a6 at 6-5 with Melmetal alive at 59/492 - one member and about one turn short. I would call it winnable-in-principle and currently unproven; on the brief's own escalation rule (three failed optimized attempts) six failures justify opening a level review.
what_that_party_needed: A body Water Spout cannot profitably hit. Storm Drain Gastrodon is the single biggest swing in the fight: Kyogre threw Water Spout 0 times in 5 opportunities while it was on the field and reverted to it the turn it died, in both games. Water Absorb (Jellicent, Clodsire, Vaporeon, Seismitoad) and Dry Skin (Toxicroak) do the same job.

A special Ground move on turn 1. Lucario's 183 Sp. Def means Earth Power OHKOs it, so Follow Me stops being a wall and becomes the thing that drags the OHKO onto the redirector. Lucario died on turn 1 in both fresh attempts, for free, whether or not Follow Me was up. Special Ground is also the only lane that ignores Iron Defense entirely.

A Ghost. Gholdengo took zero from Body Press and Close Combat, resisted Heavy Slam, Double Iron Bash, Water Spout, Ice Beam and Hurricane, and - because the roster carries no Ground and no usable Fire - had no super-effective matchup on the board except Marshadow. It was the last player Pokemon standing in both attempts.

Chi-Yu, held in reserve until Primordial Sea lifts. At 328 Speed it is faster than Zamazenta's 324; Beads of Ruin cuts every opposing Sp. Def by a quarter, and Life Orb Overheat or Heat Wave then OHKOs Lucario, Zapdos, Zamazenta, Melmetal and Marshadow. In v3-a6 one Chi-Yu killed Marshadow, contributed the lethal blow on Kyogre, and killed Zapdos and Zamazenta on consecutive turns.

Two independent guaranteed OHKOs on Kyogre, and even that is not enough. Grassy Terrain Wood Hammer (462-543) and Choice Band Leaf Blade from 348 Speed (467-549) are the two the cap-100 pool offers. v3-a6 had one and it was Protected away; v3-a7 had both and lost them to one Hurricane and two consecutive Protects.
is_it_winnable_by_a_party_built_against_.what_it_still_lacks: a way to make Kyogre's Protect cost something. Protect is +4, Prankster Taunt is +1, so the player can never pre-empt the first one, and a 419-HP / 290-Def / 370-Sp.Def body behind Follow Me is not 2HKOd by anything in the pool that is also fast enough to matter. Both of my games were decided by that one move slot.

door_still_open.which: Wide Guard held by a Ghost, on a board where BOTH actives are immune to Normal. The crack line already names it ('Wide Guard plus a Ghost so Feint cannot lift it') and no party in seven runs has actually built it.
door_still_open.why_it_is_open: Feint is .effect = EFFECT_HIT with .type = TYPE_NORMAL (src/data/moves_info.h:8511), so a Ghost target takes no damage and MOVE_EFFECT_FEINT never runs. Wide Guard and Quick Guard are exempt from the consecutive-use failure table at GEN_6+ (src/battle_move_resolution.c:1275-1283), so a Ghost can hold Wide Guard up every single turn forever. The cap-100 pool supplies Ghosts that learn it: AEGISLASH gate 42 (wild:SandstrewnRuins_B1F), DOUBLADE gate 42, LUNALA gate 54 (evolution from Cosmoem). Paired with a second Normal-immune active such as Gholdengo or Jellicent, that board blanks Water Spout and Hurricane permanently, takes zero from Body Press and Close Combat, and leaves Kyogre with nothing but a single-target Ice Beam.
door_still_open.important_caveat_the_crack_gets_wrong: one Ghost is not enough. HandleSetEffectFeint (src/battle_set_effect.c:393-417) clears the Feint target's own protection AND any side-type protection on the target's PARTNER. So Feint aimed at a non-Ghost partner still lifts the side's Wide Guard even when the Wide Guard user itself is a Ghost. The crack: line should be corrected to say both actives must be Normal-immune, or it will send a player into exactly the trap v3-a3 fell into.
door_still_open.single_change_that_closes_it: MARSHADOW's move order in the party, not its set. Marshadow is the roster's only answer to a Ghost wall - Spectral Thief and Technician Shadow Sneak are Ghost-type single-target moves that a Wide Guard slot never touches and that hit a Ghost for 2x - but as the sixth member it reached the field in only 3 of 6 games and took 4 actions in total, twice arriving on the final turn. Swapping MARSHADOW and MELMETAL in the authored order (Marshadow fifth, Melmetal sixth) puts the Ghost-breaker on the field while a Ghost wall is still doing work, costs nothing else, and does not touch a single species, move, item, ability, EV or level. Melmetal is the better last body anyway: it closed three of the six games from the sixth slot and is the roster's slowest member, so it also keeps the authored Trick Room answer in reserve where it belongs.
door_still_open.second_option_if_a_set_change_is_preferr: replace MARSHADOW's FEINT - a second copy of a move Lucario already carries, which fired zero times in seven runs and which is Normal, so it cannot break the very Ghost wall it is meant to answer - with POLTERGEIST or another Ghost/Fighting lane. FEINT is the roster's only genuinely redundant slot.

could_this_team_be_cooler: It already is, and the six games earned the claim rather than asserting it: the sea that is Primal from the first frame, a lead pair that cannot be flinched, a redirector whose Rocky Helmet punishes the very move it pulls, and two win conditions with opposite answers all showed up in play. The one slot that does not pull its weight is MARSHADOW's FEINT, a second copy of Lucario's move that never fired; and the one authored promise that has still never been tested is MELMETAL moving first under the player's Trick Room, because Melmetal is buried in the sixth slot. Both are fixed by the same reordering. No species change is warranted.
